mix_frequency_estimate: Wrap-draw class 4-way SRP OOP-early: CHECK 75% / BET 25%. 9d5d on 4d7h6c with 8 outs + BDFD: CHECK 75% / BET 25%.
reasoning:
Multiway 4-way SRP, OOP-early MP, facing UTG check, 3 villains behind (CO + BTN have position, UTG already checked). This is the structural HALT node: OOP non-PFA semi-bluff into MULTIPLE IP players behind.

Multiway semi-bluff principles:
  (1) Fold equity requirement: in HU, a small-cbet semi-bluff with 30% equity is +EV if fold equity > ~25%. In 4-way (3 villains), the compounded fold equity requirement is ~55% — i.e., ALL THREE villains must collectively fold ~55% to break even. Each villain folds maybe 50-55% to a small cbet on this connected board → 0.5^3 = 12.5% probability of all folding. Not 55%.
  (2) Realization-OOP penalty: hero is OOP-early; turn check-fold becomes hard once committed; turn check-raise from IP becomes a real threat. Bet → multiple callers → river OOP with a draw that missed is the worst outcome.
  (3) Multi-target denial: hero's 9-5 wants to deny equity from KK-JJ overcards but those hands fold for free on 4-7-6 in MW. The denial value is concentrated in folding out gutshots like 8x, 5x, 3x that retain real equity — and these hands are too sticky to fold in MW SRP (CO/BTN floating).

Board 4d7h6c specifics:
  - Highly coordinated: low straight-heavy board.
  - 3 villain ranges (UTG opener + CO MP caller + BTN late caller) collectively cover Q-Jx broadway suited (still have backdoors), 88-TT (overpair to most of board), AhTh/JhTh type FDs (no — board is rainbow, no FD), and crucially pocket pairs that flop sets (77 = 3 combos, 66 = 3 combos, 44 = 3 combos = 9 combos of set across 3 villains).
  - Two-pair density: 76, 74, 64, 75 if villains have 7-5s (rare); usually 76 (2 combos × 3 villains) and similar.
  - Made-straight density: 8-5 (need both card slots), 5-3, 3-2-A (no), so essentially 5x in CO/BTN floats. Marginal.
  - Hero is BEHIND set-density (9 combos) and TWO-PAIR density (~6 combos) and ahead of overcards/over-pairs that have no straight equity (lots of combos). Hero's effective equity vs 3-villain range ~30%.

Sibling references (same node family — 95s OOP MP wrap-class):
  - 168 (95s on 456 board, middle-pair + BDFD, MP OOP) → CHECK.
  - 190 (9c5c on 276, gutshot + BDFD, MP OOP) → CHECK.
  - 199 (9s5s on 276, gutshot + BDFD, MP OOP) → CHECK.
All three resolved CHECK with no controversy. 193 has STRONGER draw (8 outs DG vs 4-out single gut + BDFD in siblings) but the structural posture (OOP-early MP, 3 villains behind, 4-way SRP) is identical.

Counter-consideration: the BIGGER draw (8 outs vs 4 outs) does shift the mix toward BET. But:
  - 8 outs at 4-way is still only ~32% equity at the river. Hero is in the 30-40% equity bucket which is precisely the CHECK-modal bucket OOP — too thick to fold, too thin to bet for value, denial value low because the field is sticky.
  - The semi-bluff value comes from FOLD EQUITY × pot win, but fold equity vs 3 villains on a 4-7-6 board is near-zero. Each villain calls with ~70% of their range (overpairs JJ-88 don't fold, mid-pair 5s and 6s don't fold, FDs and straight draws don't fold, sets and 2P obviously don't fold). The semi-bluff is too low-FE to extract.
  - The realization-OOP penalty is enormous: hero's realization on a checked-flop pot is ~0.8 (multiway OOP), on a bet-and-called flop is ~0.55 (turn play OOP-into-2 is brutal).

Mixed-strategy: at the wrap-class node, BET frequency ~25%; CHECK 75%. The combo 9d5d sits in the modal CHECK bucket.

Verdict: CHECK at HIGH confidence. The consensus CHECK is correct. Despite the strong 8-out draw, multiway OOP-early posture dominates. BET 25-30% is a defensible minority mix but CHECK is the modal action.
